title: Positive tabindex changes the focus order
user_impact: Keyboard users reach elements in an order that does not match the page layout.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order; failure F44 (tabindex creating a tab order that does not preserve meaning); HTML §6.6.3 the tabindex attribute
checks.applicability: Rendered elements carrying a tabindex attribute that parses as an integer.
checks.expectation:
A rendered element with tabindex greater than 0 is reported once as
needs_review: a positive value moves it ahead of the natural order, which
fails 2.4.3 only when the resulting order breaks meaning or operation (F44),
and that the markup does not show. tabindex 0 and -1 keep the natural order
and are not reported; the boundary is 1. A display:none element is in no tab
order and is not reported. ARIA widgets (span role=button) and native
controls count alike, so do elements in an open shadow root, a value set by
script after load, and an element rendered on one viewport only.
